title: Exact geometric inverse image with arbitrary constant left-module coefficients
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be small sites and let $f:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ be a geometric morphism, meaning an adjunction $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$ on sheaves of sets with $f^{-1}$ preserving finite limits [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Fix a unital ring $\Lambda$, not assumed commutative, in the coefficient universe [def-weil-size-convention]. On each site let $\Lambda_{\mathcal C},\Lambda_{\mathcal D}$ be the sheafifications of the constant ring presheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and use left-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. There is a canonical ring-sheaf isomorphism $f^{-1}\Lambda_{\mathcal C}\cong\Lambda_{\mathcal D}$ carrying constant scalar sections to the same scalars. Applying $f^{-1}$ to addition, zero, negation and each scalar endomorphism defines a functor $f^*_{\Lambda}:\operatorname{Mod}(\Lambda_{\mathcal C})\to\operatorname{Mod}(\Lambda_{\mathcal D})$. This functor is exact and, writing $V$ for forgetting scalars, has a canonical natural isomorphism $Vf^*_{\Lambda}\cong f^{-1}_{\operatorname{Ab}}V$. It identifies the forgotten module adjunction unit with the abelian inverse-image unit. These identifications commute with composition of geometric morphisms and with restrictions to localized sites. Thus termwise $f^*_{\Lambda}$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms of complexes and induces inverse image on bounded-below derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories].
